demos.brief: We run a network of 6 physiotherapy clinics and want patients to book sessions online. We need SMS reminders to cut no-shows and a card deposit for first visits. Reception should see a calendar per clinic. Want to launch in spring. Our current booking is a shared spreadsheet.
demos.sources:
<sources>
<source id="b001:scope:0" title="Dental clinic booking app" outcome="delivered" actual_hours="640.0" actual_cost_usd="58000.0">
- Patient-facing web app: pick clinic, dentist and time slot, with confirmation by email.
- SMS reminders 24 hours and 2 hours before the appointment.
- Online deposit payment (card) for first visits.
- Receptionist dashboard with a day and week calendar, able to move or cancel appointments.
- Around 4,000 active patients, 12 dentists, 3 clinics.
</source>
<source id="b001:context:0" title="Dental clinic booking app" outcome="delivered" actual_hours="640.0" actual_cost_usd="58000.0">
Sorriso Group runs three dental clinics in the same city. Today receptionists book appointments by phone and a shared spreadsheet, and double bookings happen almost every week. The owner wants patients to book online and wants fewer no-shows. They have no in-house developers, only an agency that maintains their website.
</source>
<source id="b001:outcome:0" title="Dental clinic booking app" outcome="delivered" actual_hours="640.0" actual_cost_usd="58000.0">
Delivered in 640 hours against an estimate of 420. The SMS provider integration took far longer than planned: delivery receipts were unreliable and we had to add a retry queue, which doubled that part of the estimate. The CSV import from the old practice-management software caused duplicate patients and cost about 60 extra hours of cleanup rules. Payments went smoothly using a hosted checkout. No-shows dropped noticeably after launch, but we did not measure by how much. Lesson: always prototype the third-party messaging integration in week one.
</source>
<source id="b006:scope:0" title="Telemedicine platform" outcome="delivered" actual_hours="1100.0" actual_cost_usd="105000.0">
- Member login using the insurer's existing identity system.
- Doctor availability calendar and appointment booking.
- Video consultation room in the browser, no app install.
- Post-consultation notes and e-prescriptions saved to the member record.
- Admin reports on consultations per doctor.
</source>
<source id="b008:context:0" title="Loyalty app for a coffee chain" outcome="delivered" actual_hours="760.0" actual_cost_usd="70000.0">
Grão Dourado is a coffee chain with 35 stores. They run a paper stamp card and want a mobile loyalty app to see who their customers are and to send offers. Marketing owns the project and wants the first version in time for the chain's anniversary campaign.
</source>
</sources>

scope.summary: Online booking for a 6-clinic physiotherapy network: patient-facing booking, SMS reminders, card deposit for first visits, and a per-clinic reception calendar replacing a shared spreadsheet. The dental clinic booking app (b001) is a close match in features and starting point (3 clinics, spreadsheet, SMS, deposit, reception calendar). The new brief has twice as many clinics, so the range is adjusted upward. Other sources (telemedicine, coffee loyalty) are not comparable and were not used.
open_questions: Do patients pick a specific physiotherapist, or only a clinic and time slot? Are treatment types with different durations involved?
How many active patients, practitioners and appointments per week across the 6 clinics?
Is there existing patient data in the spreadsheet to migrate, and how clean is it?
Which SMS provider is preferred or already in use, and what countries or numbers must be supported?
What is the deposit amount, is it refundable or deducted from the session fee, and what is the cancellation policy?
Do patients need accounts, or can they book as guests?
Are there insurance or health-data privacy requirements (e.g. HIPAA/GDPR) for storing patient records?
Who maintains the system after launch, and is there an in-house technical team?
What is the exact spring launch date, and is a phased clinic-by-clinic rollout acceptable?
Is online booking needed to sync with any other system (billing, practice management, Google Calendar)?

risks.description: SMS provider integration is likely to take longer than planned: unreliable delivery receipts required a retry queue and doubled that part of the estimate on the comparable project. Prototype the messaging integration in week one.

citations.quote: delivery receipts were unreliable and we had to add a retry queue, which doubled that part of the estimate

risks.description: Migrating existing data from the spreadsheet could create duplicate patients and require extra cleanup rules, as happened with the CSV import on the dental project.

citations.quote: The CSV import from the old practice-management software caused duplicate patients and cost about 60 extra hours of cleanup rules.

risks.description: The comparable project overran its own estimate (640 hours vs 420), so a tight spring deadline with twice the clinics leaves little buffer.

citations.quote: Delivered in 640 hours against an estimate of 420.

risks.description: The shared spreadsheet likely allows double bookings; the new calendar must enforce per-clinic and per-practitioner availability and handle moves or cancellations to avoid conflicts during the changeover.

citations.quote: double bookings happen almost every week

risks.description: Card deposits are lower risk if a hosted checkout is used; building custom payment handling would add scope and compliance burden.

citations.quote: Payments went smoothly using a hosted checkout.

risks.description: Multi-clinic setup (6 clinics) adds configuration, per-clinic calendars, permissions and testing, and rollout/training across more sites than the reference project.

assumptions: Baseline is the actual 640 hours of the dental clinic booking app (b001), which had the same core features with 3 clinics.
Low end assumes the SMS integration is prototyped early, a hosted checkout is used, and little data migration is needed, so the 6 clinics add only modest configuration effort.

High end adds roughly 50% over the baseline for twice as many clinics, per-clinic calendars and permissions, rollout and training, and a possible repeat of SMS and data-cleanup overruns (about 60 hours of cleanup).
Excludes ongoing maintenance, SMS usage fees and payment processing fees.
Does not assume treatment-type scheduling, practitioner-level rosters, or integration with other systems; these would increase the range.

citations.quote: Online deposit payment (card) for first visits.
Delivered in 640 hours against an estimate of 420.

insufficient_info: Patient volume, practitioner count and appointment complexity for the physiotherapy network are not stated, so the scale comparison to the dental project (about 4,000 patients, 12 dentists) is uncertain.
Cost in USD is not estimated because rates and team composition for this engagement are unknown.

demos.brief: A pharmacy chain wants to offer video consultations with pharmacists and doctors in the browser, with e-prescriptions saved to the customer account. About 50 professionals will work remotely. Customer login should use our existing identity provider. Must comply with health data rules and go live in January.
demos.sources:
<sources>
<source id="b006:scope:0" title="Telemedicine platform" outcome="delivered" actual_hours="1100.0" actual_cost_usd="105000.0">
- Member login using the insurer's existing identity system.
- Doctor availability calendar and appointment booking.
- Video consultation room in the browser, no app install.
- Post-consultation notes and e-prescriptions saved to the member record.
- Admin reports on consultations per doctor.
</source>
<source id="b006:context:0" title="Telemedicine platform" outcome="delivered" actual_hours="1100.0" actual_cost_usd="105000.0">
Vida Online is a small health insurer that wants to offer video consultations to its 30,000 members. Today members call a hotline and wait days for a callback. The medical director has already signed a contract with 40 doctors who will work remotely.
</source>
<source id="b006:constraints:0" title="Telemedicine platform" outcome="delivered" actual_hours="1100.0" actual_cost_usd="105000.0">
Health data privacy law applies, so all video and notes must stay in the country. Go-live was fixed for the open enrollment period in January. The insurer's identity system uses an old SAML setup.
</source>
<source id="b001:constraints:0" title="Dental clinic booking app" outcome="delivered" actual_hours="640.0" actual_cost_usd="58000.0">
Launch before March because the owner wants it live for the spring campaign. Patient data must stay in the country. The existing practice-management software has no API, so appointments are exported as a daily CSV file.
</source>
<source id="b006:outcome:0" title="Telemedicine platform" outcome="delivered" actual_hours="1100.0" actual_cost_usd="105000.0">
Delivered in 1,100 hours against an estimate of 900. Video itself was easy using a managed video API. The overrun came from the SAML integration (about 90 hours, the insurer's test environment was down for weeks) and from compliance reviews of the prescription flow, which the client only revealed after the first demo. Load tests showed the video provider's free tier was not enough, which changed the monthly cost for the client. Lesson: ask about compliance reviews and test environments before quoting.
</source>
</sources>

scope.summary: Browser-based video consultation platform for a pharmacy chain: pharmacist and doctor consultations, e-prescriptions saved to the customer account, login through the client's existing identity provider, about 50 remote professionals, health data compliance, January go-live. A past telemedicine project (b006) is a close match in features, compliance and deadline. It took 1,100 hours / $105,000 against an estimate of 900 hours. The overrun came from identity integration and compliance reviews, so the range is weighted toward the actual outcome rather than the original estimate. The pharmacy brief adds a pharmacist role and possibly more complex prescription handling, which the past project did not cover.
open_questions: Which identity provider and protocol (SAML, OIDC) is used, and is a stable test environment available now?
Which health data rules apply (country/region, e.g. HIPAA, GDPR, local law), and must video and notes stay in-country?
Are compliance or legal reviews of the e-prescription flow required, and when can they happen (before build, or after the first demo)?
Do e-prescriptions need to be transmitted to a pharmacy system or national e-prescription registry, or only saved to the customer account?
Is appointment booking and a professional availability calendar in scope? Do pharmacists and doctors have different workflows?
What is the expected number of concurrent consultations and total customers, so the video provider tier and monthly running cost can be sized?
Which January date is the hard deadline, and is it tied to a campaign or regulatory event?
Are admin reports, notifications (email/SMS) and multi-language support in scope?
Do the 50 professionals already have identities and licences that need verification, and how will they log in?

risks.description: Identity provider integration can overrun, especially if the client's test environment is unavailable for weeks.

citations.quote: The overrun came from the SAML integration (about 90 hours, the insurer's test environment was down for weeks)

risks.description: Compliance reviews of the prescription flow may surface late and add unplanned work, threatening a fixed January go-live.

citations.quote: compliance reviews of the prescription flow, which the client only revealed after the first demo

risks.description: Health data law may require in-country hosting of video and notes, constraining the choice of video provider and infrastructure.

risks.description: The video provider's free tier may be insufficient under load, raising the client's recurring monthly cost.

risks.description: Fixed January go-live leaves little buffer if the identity or compliance work slips.

citations.quote: Go-live was fixed for the open enrollment period in January.

risks.description: Pharmacist plus doctor roles and a pharmacy chain context may add workflow, multi-site and prescription complexity beyond the past project.

assumptions: Based on b006, a comparable delivered telemedicine project at 1,100 actual hours (estimate had been 900).
Low end assumes the identity provider has a working test environment and the compliance requirements are known up front, close to the b006 actual.
High end adds about 25% for the extra pharmacist role, more professionals (50 vs 40), and compliance or identity delays.
Assumes a managed video API is used and the video provider's paid tier is budgeted separately as a running cost.
Excludes the provider's monthly fees and any legal or compliance consulting fees.

Post-consultation notes and e-prescriptions saved to the member record.

demos.brief: Our furniture shop is on an old custom-built website that crashes during sales. We want to move to a modern ecommerce platform without losing our Google ranking. Around 4,000 products with variants like color and size, plus customer and order history. Stock must stay in sync with our physical stores through their old inventory system.
demos.sources:
<sources>
<source id="b002:context:0" title="Shoe retailer store migration" outcome="delivered" actual_hours="900.0" actual_cost_usd="79000.0">
Passo Certo sells shoes online and in 14 physical stores. Their online shop runs on a custom PHP system written eight years ago by a freelancer who is no longer around. It is slow during sales and nobody dares to change it. They asked us to move the shop to a modern platform without losing their search ranking.
</source>
<source id="b002:scope:0" title="Shoe retailer store migration" outcome="delivered" actual_hours="900.0" actual_cost_usd="79000.0">
- Migrate catalog (about 6,000 products with sizes and colors), customers and order history.
- New storefront with the existing visual identity.
- Integration with the payment gateway and with the stock system used by the stores, so online stock matches physical stock.
- Redirects for all old product URLs.
- Admin training for the marketing team.
</source>
<source id="b002:outcome:0" title="Shoe retailer store migration" outcome="delivered" actual_hours="900.0" actual_cost_usd="79000.0">
Delivered in 900 hours against an estimate of 650. Product data was much messier than the client said: sizes were free text in the old database, and normalizing them took around 140 hours. The stock integration was the main risk and it did hurt: the SOAP API rate-limited us and stock could be 10 to 15 minutes late, which we accepted after agreeing it with the client. The cutover itself took 90 minutes of downtime. Search ranking dipped for two weeks and then recovered because of the redirect map. Lesson: audit the data quality before quoting a migration.
</source>
<source id="b009:scope:0" title="Inventory forecasting dashboard" outcome="delivered" actual_hours="520.0" actual_cost_usd="47500.0">
- Load three years of sales history from the retailer's ERP export (CSV files nightly).
- Weekly demand forecast per product and per region using standard time-series methods.
- Dashboard with forecast vs actual and suggested order quantities.
- Buyers can override a suggestion and leave a comment.
</source>
<source id="b010:scope:0" title="B2B wholesale ordering portal" outcome="delivered" actual_hours="1250.0" actual_cost_usd="118000.0">
- Customer accounts with company-specific price lists and credit limits.
- Catalog with 3,000 products, reorder from previous orders, CSV upload of large orders.
- Approval flow for orders above the credit limit.
- Integration with the ERP to create orders and read stock and invoices.
- Invoice download and payment status.
</source>
</sources>

scope.summary: Migrate a furniture shop with about 4,000 products (color/size variants), customer and order history from a crashing custom-built site to a modern ecommerce platform. The migration must preserve Google ranking through redirects and keep stock in sync with the physical stores' legacy inventory system. The closest comparable is the Passo Certo shoe retailer migration (b002), which had the same shape: custom legacy shop, variants, customers and orders, store stock integration, and SEO preservation. It took 900 hours against an initial estimate of 650. This project has fewer products (4,000 vs 6,000), so the range is adjusted slightly downward, but with a wide upper bound because of data-quality and legacy-integration risk.
open_questions: What is the quality of the product data? Are variants (color, size) structured fields or free text? Can we audit a sample before fixing the quote?
What is the legacy inventory system (vendor, version) and what interface does it offer (API, SOAP, database, file export)? Are there rate limits?
How fresh must stock be online? Is a delay of 10 to 15 minutes acceptable, or is real-time sync required?
How many physical stores feed stock into the system, and do they sell the same stock pool as online?
Which target platform is preferred or already chosen (Shopify, Magento, WooCommerce, etc.)?
How many customers and orders need to be migrated, and how far back does history go?
Is the existing visual identity to be kept, or is a new storefront design needed?
Which payment gateways and shipping integrations are required?
How many old URLs are indexed, and is there any current SEO tooling or analytics access?
What traffic peaks occur during sales, and what load must the new platform handle?
What downtime window is acceptable for cutover?
Is admin training for staff required?

risks.description: Product data quality is likely worse than the client believes. In the shoe migration, free-text sizes took around 140 hours to normalize. Furniture variants (color, size, materials) may have similar problems.

citations.quote: sizes were free text in the old database, and normalizing them took around 140 hours

risks.description: Integration with the old inventory system may be rate-limited or slow, leaving online stock late relative to the physical stores and risking overselling. The client must agree on an acceptable delay.

citations.quote: the SOAP API rate-limited us and stock could be 10 to 15 minutes late

risks.description: Search ranking may dip after cutover even with a redirect map, which would affect revenue in the short term. A complete redirect map for all old URLs is essential.

citations.quote: Search ranking dipped for two weeks and then recovered because of the redirect map.

risks.description: Legacy custom code with no documentation or original developer makes it hard to understand data structures and business rules, which may lead to underestimation.

citations.quote: custom PHP system written eight years ago by a freelancer who is no longer around

risks.description: Cutover causes some downtime and could coincide with a sales event if poorly planned. Schedule it away from peak sales periods.

citations.quote: The cutover itself took 90 minutes of downtime.

assumptions: Based mainly on b002, a very similar shoe retailer migration that took 900 hours (initially estimated at 650).
Catalog is smaller (about 4,000 vs 6,000 products), so the lower bound is set near the original 650-hour estimate.
The upper bound allows for the same data-cleaning and stock integration problems seen in b002, with slightly more effort allowed for the furniture variant structure.
The legacy inventory system has a usable interface and a stock delay of 10 to 15 minutes is acceptable.
Scope includes catalog, customer and order history migration, storefront on an existing visual identity, payment gateway, stock integration, redirects and basic admin training.
A data-quality audit before the final quote could narrow the range.
b010 and b009 were not used because they are different project types.

citations.quote: Delivered in 900 hours against an estimate of 650.
Integration with the payment gateway and with the stock system used by the stores, so online stock matches physical stock.
